title: A1 Writing Quiz 8 — Health, Weather & Free Time

questions.question: Choose the correct word order.
options: Every day water I drink lots of.
I drink lots of water every day.
I lots of water drink every day.
Drink I lots of water every day.
questions.explanation: Subject + verb + object + time: 'I drink lots of water every day.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word order.
options: The doctor works at a clinic.
The doctor at a clinic works.
Works the doctor at a clinic.
At a clinic the doctor works.
questions.explanation: Subject + verb + place: 'The doctor works at a clinic.'

questions.question: Choose the correct word order.
questions.explanation: Subject + verb + object: 'She has a bad headache.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question word order.
questions.explanation: Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + verb: 'How do you feel today?'

questions.question: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
questions.explanation: Days of the week (Sundays) and the pronoun 'I' are always capitalized.

questions.question: Choose the correctly capitalized sentence.
options: it is very cold in january in baku.
It is very cold in January in Baku.
It Is very cold in january in baku.
it is very Cold in January in Baku.
questions.explanation: Month names (January) and city names (Baku) are proper nouns and must be capitalized.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
questions.explanation: A simple statement ends with a full stop: 'I feel better today.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
questions.explanation: A question ends with a question mark: 'Is it sunny today?'

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct commas.
options: I like swimming football and chess.
I like swimming, football and chess.
I like, swimming football, and chess.
I like swimming, football, and, chess.
questions.explanation: Use commas to separate items in a list: 'swimming, football and chess.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'I'm' is the contraction of 'I am'.

questions.question: My grandfather ___ a walk every morning.
questions.explanation: Present simple with 'grandfather' (he) takes -s: 'takes'.

questions.question: I ___ ill last weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Last weekend' signals past simple; past of 'am' is 'was'.

questions.question: Look at the sky! It ___ to snow.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' signals an action happening now → present continuous: 'is starting'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'and'.
options: I feel tired and I feel hungry.
I feel tired and but hungry.
questions.explanation: 'And' joins two similar feelings: 'I feel tired and I feel hungry.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'but'.
options: The weather is cold but sunny.
The weather is cold and but sunny.
But the weather is cold sunny.
The weather, sunny but is cold.
questions.explanation: 'But' shows contrast: 'The weather is cold but sunny.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'so'.
options: I had a headache, so I took some medicine.
So I had a headache I took medicine.
I had a headache I took so medicine.
So, took I medicine headache had.
questions.explanation: 'So' introduces a result: 'I had a headache, so I took some medicine.'

questions.question: The pharmacy is ___ the hospital and the park.
questions.explanation: 'Between' describes a position among two things: 'between the hospital and the park.'

questions.question: I usually feel sleepy ___ the afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'In' is used with parts of the day: 'in the afternoon.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'Aspirin' starts with a vowel sound /æ/ → 'an aspirin.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start a message telling a friend you are sick?
questions.explanation: 'Hi [Name],' is the correct informal greeting for a friend.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a message wishing a friend to get well soon?
questions.explanation: 'Get well soon, [Name]' is a caring, informal closing suitable for a friend who is ill.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start a formal email requesting a doctor's appointment?
questions.explanation: 'Dear Doctor [Surname],' is a respectful, semi-formal opening when the name is known.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'I like sunny days.' and 'I like warm weather.'?
options: I like sunny days but warm weather.
I like sunny days and warm weather.
I like sunny days, I like warm weather.
I sunny days and warm weather like.
questions.explanation: Two related likes can be joined simply: 'I like sunny days and warm weather.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She wore a woolen warm hat.
She wore a warm woolen hat.
She wore warm a woolen hat.
She wore a hat warm woolen.
questions.explanation: Opinion/quality adjectives come before material: 'a warm woolen hat.'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly shows relief?
questions.explanation: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling of relief: 'I feel much better now!'

questions.question: ___ a strong wind today.
questions.explanation: 'A strong wind' is singular → 'There is'.

questions.question: This is ___ tennis racket. (belongs to my coach)
questions.explanation: Singular possessive: add apostrophe + s → "coach's tennis racket".

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, I warm up. Then, I go for a run.
First I warm up then go run.
Go for a run first then warm I up.
Then first, I warm the go up run.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words like 'First,' and 'Then,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: The doctors and the nurses ___ helpful.
questions.explanation: Compound subject ('The doctors and the nurses') is plural → 'are'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: Wh-phrase + auxiliary + subject + verb: 'What sport do you like?'
